environment: User’s M3, visible inline Chromium 157; Apple WebGPU / metal-3, fallback false; luma 10.0.0-alpha.15
scope: Isolated cluster centroids, attraction and integration; 8, 1,024 and 8,192 points.
question: Can WebGPU preserve Cosmos cluster attraction and its update semantics at useful cost?
method: Unchanged production GLSL, grouped high/low WebGPU reduction and corrected arithmetic, independent scalar CPU reference.
conclusion: Cluster attraction passes the bounded comparison through 8,192 points. WebGPU is faster for one large or heavily uneven group; WebGL has lower medians for balanced groups and supplied targets.

checks.name: Backend versus CPU
checks.detail: 45/45 checkpoint/update rows per backend, including group sums, force, integration and independent positions.

checks.name: WebGPU versus WebGL
checks.detail: 18/18 comparisons from identical inputs; 18/18 post-timing group sums also pass.

checks.name: Force-only GPU cost
checks.detail: 126 measured batches plus 36 warmups. Results depend on group shape; they do not measure full frames.

limits: One native session, 30 ticks, fixed alpha, four checkpoints and one membership/target/strength update per input. Combined forces, long trajectories, production setters, update latency and whole-frame cost remain unchecked. Pilot picking and color failures remain open.
visual: Live positions evolve separately. The preview is a new local session, not recorded evidence.
